title: New Year's Eve - the Sudoku
description:
Try James Kopp's excellent NYE Sudoku here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hmRBD2d4jf


Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along yellow thermometers from the bulb to the end(s). Clues outside the grid show the total of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats. Blue, green and purple 'balloons' are odd digits.

title: A New Year Miracle
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle is a gem by Scott Strosahl - it's called The New Year Miracle, which seems a fitting hope for these times.  You can play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3P74TRJGFP

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku Rules apply but, instead of the usual 3x3 boxes, each irregularly-shaped 9 cell region must contain the digits 1 to 9.  Digits in two orthogonally adjacent cells may not be consecutive.  Cells separated by a knight’s move or a king’s move in chess cannot contain the same digit.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage.

**************************************************************

We have released a brand new sudoku puzzle hunt for our patrons on Patreon!  This one has been made by Stéphane Bura and Akash Jain and it's awesome.  You can also find The Modern Art Sudoku Pack and a new sudoku from Mark:

description:

title: The NEW Miracle Sudoku
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle is quite ridiculously clever - look at it - how can it have only one solution?!  It's called Dotless Kropki Sudoku X and it's by Phistomefel but we call it The New Miracle Sudoku....you can play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rLNbnB6FnD

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku Rules apply. The two main diagonals each contain every number from 1 to 9 exactly once. The numbers of two orthogonally adjacent squares may not be consecutive, nor may they be in a ratio of 2:1.

title: The 8Min 30Sec Puzzle Challenge
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle is an absolute beauty by the awesome constructor from Germany, Jonas Gleim.  It's called Checkered Fillomino and it's well worth your time (although the grandmaster solve time for this is 8m30s... good luck!).  Play it at the link below:

https://tinyurl.com/y79sa9n2

Rules:  
Divide the grid into regions and place a number in each cell. The numbers within a region must all be the same and equal to the size of the region. Regions of equal size must not touch orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. A region may contain zero, one or more of the given numbers.  In addition, it must be possible to shade some regions fully, such that two shaded regions or two unshaded regions never touch orthogonally.

The puzzle was published on GMpuzzles.com - a super source of handcrafted content.  This is their website:

title: The 'Friends' Sudoku!
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle is called Why Can't We Be Friends and it's a collaboration between SlowLarry and Philip Newman - it's also brilliant.  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8mrQmDf69T

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A friendly cell has a value identical to its row-, column- or box-number, counted in the standard way. The green "lawn" cells are friendly. (For example, r1c7 must be either 1 to match the row, 3 to match the box, or 7 to match the column.)  Additionally, an orthogonally-connected one-cell wide path (so the path cannot touch itself orthogonally) must be found between the cells marked with circles, such that every cell on the path - including the marked cells - is friendly but not lawn. (Note: there could be friendly cells other than path or lawn in the puzzle.)  Along the marked arrows, the digits in the friendly cells (any friendly cells - whether lawn, path, or otherwise) sum to the same total as the digits in the cells that are not friendly.

title: The Night Before Christmas Sudoku
description:
Try Jonny Kaufman’s exciting Night Before Christmas Sudoku here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/B87B8q8m2q

Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each row/column begins with a number X, and 1 is the Xth cell of that row/column. Draw Santa’s path in the grid that starts and ends with the two circles. Santa travels orthogonally, and the path may not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally, nor enter the red region, nor contain a 1. Grey cells (houses) are not part of Santa’s path. Their number inside (never 1) indicates how many of the surrounding 8 cells are part of Santa’s path. Not all possible houses are given. Santa’s path totals 165.

title: The Most Complex Sudoku Ever
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle must be the most complex we've ever covered on CtC!  It is by Philip Newman and it's called Advent Of Sudoku.  Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8M7Hdm6pNG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot appear in the same position in different 3x3 boxes. In box 1: Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. (No negative constraint.) In box 2: Digits along the thermometer must increase from the bulb end. In box 3: Digits along the indicated diagonal sum to the given total. In box 4: Digits in the circle must appear in one of the surrounding four cells. In box 5: Digits separated by an X must sum to 10; digits separated by an V must sum to 5. (No negative constraint.) In box 6: Digits along the arrow must sum to the circled digit. In box 7: Digits in the cage must sum to the given total. In box 8: Digits in a circle must be odd. In box 9: Digits separated by a black dot must have a 2:1 ratio. (No negative constraint.)

[Simon goes through the rules in detail at the start of the video if you are unfamiliar with any of those outlined above.]

title: Pretty Little Liars: The Sudoku!
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle is by DiMono and it's called Everything Is Wrogn!  A metaphor for these strange times...  Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jL24HLphHb

Rules:  [Get ready, these are special...!]
Normal sudoku rules apply. However, every clue is lying to you! The thermometer bulb is not where it says it is (but is still on the thermo, and each thermo cannot contain a repeated digit).   Killer cages don't sum to the number in the corner. Little killer arrows do not give the sum of cells on their diagonal. X and V clues mean the adjoining cells don't add to 10 or 5 respectively. The palindrome line does not contain a palindrome. Black kropki dots mean neither adjoining cell is half of the other. Maximum cells (in blue) are not greater than all four adjacent cells.; Cells touching “quadruple circles” do not include all digits within the circle (but may include some of them).

NB If you are unfamiliar with any of these rules, here is a short synopsis of some of the rules above to explain how they work normally:
Thermo:  Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
Killer: In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat in a cage.
Palindrome: Along a line, the string of digits must read the the same forwards and backwards.

We are using new software at the moment so if the above link gives you any trouble you can use the old software here:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/jL24HLphHb

description:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GHr3MNpNBd

Rules:  Normal Sudoku rules apply. Some cells have to be coloured grey. All grey cells have to be orthogonally connected. All white cells have to be orthogonally connected, as well. title: Struggling through Christmas
description:
Try Joseph Nehme's puzzle here and beat Mark's time: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3dNFBmgmBp


Normal sudoku rlues apply, and identical digits cannot be a chess knight's move apart. The grey square marks an even digit. Any two cages that share an edge and whose totals have a difference of 1 have a white dot between them, and any two cages that share an edge whose totals have a ratio of 2:1 have a black dot between them; there is a negative constraint so two cages touching each other without a dot do not have totals with a difference of 1 or a ratio of 2:1.

title: Let Sudoku Ease Your Troubled Mind
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle is by Glum Hippo but there's nothing glum about it - it's called A Bouquet Of Arrows 4 and has a 100% rating on Logic Masters Germany!  Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4bJmfhdd9f

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  The digits along an arrow sum either to the number in the circle (x) or to the square of that number (x times x). The circled digit does not contribute to its own sum. There are also 3 instances of paired cells in a circle (pill). Here, the two cells should be read as a two digit number, reading from left to right.

Glum Hippo logo art by Miriam Martincic: https://www.miriamdraws.com/

description:

One of the interesting things about this puzzle is that it LOOKS like it should be easy but... it really isn't! title: The Cells Of Schrödinger
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

Today's puzzle is by SlowLarry (also known as ryokousha on our Discord server) and it's an extremely original gem!  You can play the puzzle here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/BNjgbtG62b

Rules:  
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage.  A “friendly” cell has a value identical to its row-, column- or box-number, counted in the standard way.  Green cells are friendly. Eg Row1Column8 could be a 1 (row), 8 (column) or 3 (box).  R9c2 could be an 9 (row), 2 (column) or 7 (box).

Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by:

 - a V sum to 5

title: The Square Necessities!
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

Today's puzzle is a debut from Jeff Wajes and not only is it very clever it's a lot of fun!  You can play the puzzle here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/mr6QBMf8HN

Rules:  
Normal Sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  An odd snake has made the grid its home! You must deduce the cells where the snake begins and ends. The snake has the following properties: the snake's body consists solely of odd digit cells; the snake visits all 9 boxes; the snake does not touch itself orthogonally (Diagonals are fine); the snake does not orthogonally touch any odd digit cell that is not part of its body (Diagonals are fine).

The puzzle was published on Logic Masters Germany here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0004VF

title: One Of The All-Time Great Puzzles
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

We had a request from a top-class solver to see if we could find a way to solve this incredible puzzle by SirWoezel...  Do we manage or did we bifurcate?  Watch the video to see!  You can play the puzzle here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/bPgHhFJdm4

Rules:  
Normal Sudoku rules apply.  Normal Killer Sudoku rules apply ie digits don't repeat in cages and the digits in a cage add up to the number given in the top left cell. The entire grid has to be filled with cages, each must be at least 2 cells large. The sum of a cage may already be given (question marks indicate an unknown sum, which may be any number of digits). The sum of each cage is given in the leftmost cage cell of the highest row in which the cage makes an appearance.  Every cage must contain exactly one circle. The digit in the circle is equal to the size of the cage. Two different cages with the same size may not share a row or a column. 

The puzzle was published on Logic Masters Germany here:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003QT

title: Don't Let Your Snake Touch Itself!
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

The Sudoku Professor, Richard Stolk, has made a really clever palindromic snake sudoku as No.297 in his Sudoku Variant Series.  You can play it here: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/rJt3468PBN

Rules:  
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Draw a snake in the grid that starts and ends in the cells with the circles. The snake wriggles horizontally and vertically and never touches itself, not even diagonally. The digits on the snake form a palindrome ie they read backwards the same as forwards. The digits in grey cells are not part of the snake and indicate how many of the horizontally, vertically and diagonally adjacent cells are part of the snake. All possible grey cells are given.



The puzzle was published on Logic Masters Germany here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0004UJ

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/3nt2JnrRPL

Normal sudoku rules apply. The nine grey cells and each main diagonal must also contain the digits 1 to 9.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.  Digits may repeat along these diagonals. Four cells touched by a red diamond must sum to an even number.

title: When One Genius Inspires Another...
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

Today's puzzle is by the great Phistomefel and he was inspired by another genius compiler ahaupt!  This means this puzzle is full of genius, which is daunting...!  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/9qMJNmR7Gj

Rules:    
Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, some cells must be coloured grey. Grey cells may not be orthogonally adjacent and the non-gray cells have to form an orthogonally-connected set. All cells (grey and non-grey) must, as usual, contain a digit. A number in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits that are “seen” from this cell looking to the north, south, east and west. The cell with the clue counts once in this sum. Grey cells block the visibility. A cell with a clue may not be coloured grey. Within the field of vision of a clue, digits may repeat if the sudoku rules allow it. 



Check out the example of how the puzzle works at this link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0004SG

title: The Best Kakuro EVER!
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

Today's puzzle is a kakuro variant by Genomico (thanks to Glum Hippo for the recommendation).  It is a simply gorgeous creation and we urge everyone to give it a go!  You can play the puzzle here:


https://git.io/JUgwF


Rules:    

Fill some white cells using digits 1-9, such that the sum of each block of digits equals the clues in the grey cells. A clue above a diagonal applies to the block of digits to its right. A clue beneath a diagonal applies to the block of digits below it. Within a block all digits are different. Some cells remain empty. All empty cells are traversed by a single closed loop that travels horizontally and vertically and doesn’t cross or overlap itself.


Advice for using the software interface for today's puzzle: The "Tab" option can be used to adjust what the Tab button does on the keyboard.  If you tick Surface/Line – normal/Candidates then you can Tab between these functions to allow you to shade/draw the loop/enter digits respectively.



**************************************************************

Try Wessel Strijkstra’s Secret Skyscraper Sudoku here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/htFgPjhFp2 
 
Normal sudoku rules apply, and dots connect cells that have a ratio of 1:2 (black) or a difference of 1 (white). Assuming each cell is filled with a tower block of the height of its digit, clues outside the grid show how many blocks can be seen from that direction. Each letter represents a different number.

title: The Sudoku You Asked Us To Solve!
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

We've had a lot of requests to solve this one... it's by the genius Phistomefel and boy-oh-boy is it a mental workout!  You can play the puzzle here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/GBfd7PptH8


Rules:    
[Note there is an example puzzle/solution on Logic Masters Germany which would be worth looking at - see link below - if you are unsure about any of the following].


Normal sudoku rules apply.  An arrow starts its growth from a cell with a circle and spreads out from there in the form of a path which is one-cell wide and neither crosses nor touches itself orthogonally. The digits on the path (without the circle) must add up to the number in the circle. Two-digit numbers in a circle are read from left to right and the arrow can start from the 'ones' digit or the 'tens' digit. All circles are given and two arrows must not intersect anywhere. A white cell must be part of exactly one arrow; a blue cell cannot contain an arrow; and an orange cell can be part of an arrow or not.


https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0004QJ



**************************************************************

Congratulations to Clover, who Sam has chosen as the winner of the competition to solve his barbaric puzzle.  If you've not tried it, you can play it at the link here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/br7MDtjjHq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat in a cage.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells on the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along the diagonal.

Sam has made a video demonstrating the solution path to the puzzle, which patrons of the channel can watch here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

title: Party Time Sudoku!
description:
Try GlumHippo's Parity Party Palindrome Sudoku here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/7Jrg7g4FMF 
 
Normal sudoku rules apply, and the two lines in the grid are palindromes (on which the same sequence of numbers runs both ways along the line). Outside the grid are Parity Party clues, which show the sum of the digits seen from that direction up to and including the first change of parity (odd/even).



Artwork for the Glum Hippo icon by the super-talented Miriam Martincic.
https://www.miriamdraws.com/

title: When a Solve Goes Horribly Wrong ...
description:
Try Cam Dennis’s The Killer in the Mirror Sudoku here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/T4Tm8DN6PM 
 
Normal sudoku rules apply, and cages show the sum of their digits and cannot include repeats. Each digit from 1-9 has a “buddy” which appears in the cell with its co-ordinates swapped – so if 1 and 4 are ‘buddies’, a 1 in r1c3 must be matched by a 4 in r3c1, and a 4 in r6c9 must be matched by a 1 in r9c6. This constraint applies to every digit in the grid. A digit’s ‘buddy’ can be itself.

title: The Sudoku of the One True Path
description:
Try Jermey Butler’s Pentomino Loop Sudoku here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/2DTRn7hQqH  
 
Normal Sudoku Rules apply. 10 different pentominos must be placed in the grid, not over given digits. Each pentomino touches exactly two other pentominos orthogonally and they form a loop, so a path could be traced orthogonally around all 10, but each pentomino may only touch another on one edge of one cell. Pentominos act as killer cages in which digits may not repeat, and corner clues in the grid indicate the sum of the pentomino’s digit or its shape.



As mentioned in our videos, do try our competition puzzle by Sam Cappleman-Lynes - it is brilliant and also HARD! 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/br7MDtjjHq

Rules:    
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in cages cannot repeat, and must sum to the total in the upper left corner of each cage. title: This Sudoku's Difficulty? A Mad 11/10!
description:
▶ KICKSTARTER LINK◀

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits?ref=docedl

Thanks to everyone who has helped with our Kickstarter Campaign to create the greatest sudoku book in history.  Check out the new stretch goals and please help us get there if you can - just days left!

Today's sudoku is a debut on the channel from Botaku.... and, let's just say, this is a mind-blowing puzzle of epic and brutal proportions.  You can play the puzzle here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/P4fBQGPP64

Rules:    
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells along the indicated diagonal.  Digits may repeat along these diagonals. In addition, the grid contains two sets of clones: 8 little clones, all identical, which consist of 3 cells; and 3 big clones, all identical, which consist of 5 cells. Clones have an orthogonally connected shape, no two clones overlap. Digits on little clones cannot be the same if they are separated by a knight's move (in chess); the big clones do not touch one another orthogonally but each of them touches a different number of little clones orthogonally. Finally, the grey cell belongs to one of the clones.

**************************************************************

title: Pac-man Returns!
description:
Try Stavros's fun Pac-man Sudoku puzzle here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/R9h8LBHngd 


Beginning in the yellow cell, create a 1-cell wide path that cannot cross itself or touch itself orthogonally, but can touch itself diagonally; the path must alternate between circles and coloured cells (beginning with yellow) until all circles and all coloured cells are taken.  The grey cells are walls. The digit in a wall cell indicates the number of path cells in the 8 cells around that wall.
Circle cells are different odd digits, square cells (the 4 coloured cells) are different even digits.  Row 5 and Column 5 wrap around, meaning the path can pass through one end and come out on the other side (like in Pac-Man).

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of their cage.  Digits cannot repeat within cages. description:
▶ KICKSTARTER LINK◀

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits?ref=docedl

Thanks to everyone who has helped with our Kickstarter Campaign to create the greatest sudoku book in history.  Check out tonight's NEW stretch goals! Please support us if you can and please remember to vote for the 10 puzzles you'd like to see in the book (you can do this on kickstarter).

**********************************************************************

▶Today's Puzzle◀

Happy Halloween!  Today's sudoku is another wonderful thematic affair from Ricky Cruz - "Trick Or Treat".  You can play it here:


https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/MLPrTD2pB6


Rules:  (Note that there are some fantastic thematic rules below but it might be easier if you're solving in our software to use the formal rules, which come first.)    


Formal rules: 

Normal sudoku rules apply.  Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.  Create a one-cell wide path in the grid to form a single loop that starts and ends in the central cell. The path must orthogonally touch each grey cell at least once but cannot enter any grey cell. The path cannot touch itself orthogonally. The central cell contains the lowest digit that can appear on the path. The path must visit each of the cells with a circle in them on them in strictly ascending order along the path (a cell is "visited" the first time the path orthogonally touches the cell). 


Flavourtext rules:
It's Halloween; time to plan your trick-or-treat route through the neighborhood!
Normal sudoku rules apply; you're a dragon for Halloween this year, and dragons don't like knights! So if two cells are a chess knight's move apart, they cannot have the same digit.
Create a one-cell wide path around the neighborhood that orthogonally touches every house at least once, starting and ending at your house in the center cell.
The path cannot touch itself orthogonally, and cannot go through any house (except your house, of course). No cell on the path can be lower than the number in your house.
Finally, the houses that have candy on them must be visited along the path in strictly ascending order (a house is visited the first time the path orthogonally touches the house). It is up to you to determine in what direction the path runs.


**************************************************************

title: "One Of The Best Puzzles I Ever Saw"
description:
▶ KICKSTARTER LINK◀

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits?ref=docedl

Thanks to everyone who has helped with our Kickstarter Campaign to create the greatest sudoku book in history.  Check out tonight's new stretch goals and please help us get there if you can and please remember to vote for the 10 puzzles you'd like to see in the book!

**********************************************************************



▶Today's Puzzle◀

Today's sudoku has garnered extraordinary praise (the title is the feedback from SirWoezel - himself a brilliant puzzlemaker) and that's why we've decided it's worth taking on this complex ruleset!  The puzzle is by Matyas Martinka and it's a complete gem - you can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/LJQfd6G3JQ

Rules:    

Normal sudoku rules apply and some snakes are hiding in the grid. A snake has a one-cell wide path. The head and tail cell of each snake need to be determined. A snake can touch itself diagonally but cannot touch itself orthogonally or revisit any cell twice. The cells not covered by snakes form exactly 8 orthogonally connected areas in the grid, one of each size from 1 cell to 8 cells. These areas are called 'snake eggs'. Each egg of size n contains the digits from 1 to n exactly once. Eggs must not touch orthogonally, but they might touch diagonally. The given digits in the grid indicate the position of the highest number of each snake egg. The snakes must connect to each other to form a single orthogonally connected area of snake cells, where no 2x2 region is covered entirely by snakes. Separate snakes might orthogonally connect anywhere, including the head cells. The head and tail cell of each snake must contain the same digit. (This digit might be different for different snakes.) Digits along the snake are not restricted: they might repeat, and the digit in the snake's head cell might be found elsewhere on the snake.

**************************************************************

title: The Miracle Arithmetic Sudoku
description:
▶ KICKSTARTER LINK◀

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits?ref=docedl


Thanks to everyone who has helped with our Kickstarter Campaign to create the greatest sudoku book in history.  Check out tonight's new stretch goals and please help us get there if you can!

**********************************************************************
▶Today's Puzzle◀


Today's sudoku has been getting rave reviews from everybody and, having now solved it, it also gets a rave review from us!  Senator Gronk has produced a stunning puzzle and you can play it here:


https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/mf8tfG3jjP

Rules:    

Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Each cage has a different sum. Let's call X the smallest sum of a cage in the puzzle and Y the largest sum of a cage in the puzzle. The cage with a sum of X is orthogonally adjacent to the cage with a sum of Y. Every number between X and Y is the sum of a cage in the puzzle. If two cages have sums that are consecutive integers, then they must be orthogonally adjacent.  Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Numbers in a thermometer must increase starting at the bulb.

title: The Sudoku With No Digits.  At All.
description:
▶ KICKSTARTER LINK◀

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits?ref=docedl

After an amazing first couple of days, we have hit the target to make the book!  Now we just hope we can reach the stretch goals to include the new puzzles!!  Please help us get there if you can!

**********************************************************************

▶Today's Puzzle◀

Today's puzzle looks incredibly daunting - no digits anywhere - but the author, udukos, was worried we'll find it too easy!!  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/QmPQnPpPQB

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits may not repeat within a cage. Within every 3*3 box (marked by thick black lines), all the killer cages have the same sum. Also, killer cage sums are unique for every 3*3 box i.e if box 1 (top left box) had killer cages each of which sum up to 10, then none of the other boxes can have killer cages with a sum of 10. The killer cage sums are not given and have to be deduced.

title: Ace Your SATs With The Sudoku Teacher!
description:
▶ KICKSTARTER LAUNCH LINK◀

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits?ref=docedl



***************************************

Today we feature the latest puzzle from RockyRoer, the American maths teacher and it's another humdinger.  You can play it here:


https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/dLT2fM8ddJ


Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat in a cage.  In addition, every cage contains kropki dots that must be located by the solver. A black dot between two cells means that one of the digits in the cells is exactly double the other. A white dot between two cells means that the two digits in the cells must be consecutive. The exact number of dots of each type are the digits in the cage sum total. For example, a 21 means there are either 2 black dots and 1 white dot or 2 white dots and 1 black dot. Within a cage, all possible kropki dots would have to be given. Dots between a 1 and 2 could count for either black or white.

title: Inspector Morse Solves Sudoku
description:
Try James Kopp's Crime Scene here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/L8LDQdbmm8


Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers increase from the bulb end of the 
thermometers. Cells separated by a white circle are consecutive. Cells 

separated by a black circle are in the ratio 1 to 2. Completing the dots between neighbouring yellow cells will allow you to detect the weapon and murderer, using Morse code (white = dot, black = dash). Morse Code: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morse_code 


Full preamble:

The sudoku shows a crime scene. On the yellow, green and white tiles lies a dagger and the splattering of blood. Some blood has been removed by the murderer before he fled the area. Help Detective Kropki uncover the method of the murder and the perpetrator of the crime.
 
On the green tiles, the blood splatter can be read as Morse Code to reveal the murder weapon. Black circles represent dashes and white circles represent dots.
 
Solve the sudoku and then insert the missing black and white circles on the yellow tiles to reveal the criminal’s identity using Morse Code. (Only circles between horizontally adjacent green cells or horizontally adjacent yellow cells are used for the Morse Code).
 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers increase from the bulb end of the thermometers. Cells separated by a white circle are consecutive. Cells separated by a black circle are in the ratio 1 to 2.

title: We Expose The Sudoku Murderer!
description:
Today's puzzle is called CluedoKu, a mash-up of Cluedo and Sudoku, by Ricky Cruz.  Two of the suspects look familiar...  Can you find out who committed the crime?  Play the puzzle here:


https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/jh6RDHdBmq


Rules: 

[Note the puzzle can be treated in two ways:  As a normal sudoku (Formal Rules below) or as the murder mystery (Flavourtext rules below).]


Flavourtext rules: 

Welcome to Sudoku Manor, where normal sudoku rules apply! Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb... except for the digit in the central cell of the grid which is "broken", meaning its thermo functions without that digit but not with it.  (The broken cell may therefore repeat a digit from elsewhere on that thermo.) The murder occurred in one of the six 3x3 "rooms" (the upper and lower 3x3 boxes). The thermos in these rooms represent the six weapons, each of which is identified by the number in the center of its room. The six suspects are gathered in the centre room, represented by the colored cells. Each suspect's cell contains a number corresponding to one of the weapons; this shows which room each suspect was in at the time of the murder. The number in the broken cell of the central thermo is the key to discovering the killer; the killer was in the only room where the highest digit on that room's thermo equals the broken cell (other rooms' thermos are allowed to share highest digits). Can you crack this cryptic case?


Normal rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb. The marked square on the central thermo is "broken", meaning the thermo functions without that digit, but not with it. The broken cell may repeat a digit from elsewhere on the thermo. The center squares of the upper and lower 3x3 boxes contain all of the digits in the coloured squares of the central 3x3 box. The digit in the broken square of the central thermo is equal to the highest digit of exactly one of the other six thermos.


The Weapons (listed in ascending order of weapon numbers!):
Candlestick
Dagger
Lead Pipe
Revolver
Rope
Wrench

title: When Sudoku Meets Chess...!
description:
Today's sudoku challenge is just really, really clever!  It's by the constructor udukos and you can play it here:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/webapp/7TbrLjNJq4


Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits may not repeat within a cage and the clue in the top left corner of a cage indicates the sum of all the digits in that cage. Also, note the inequality sign in the grid. (The killer cage without the sum is not required for the solution. It's just there to maintain the symmetry.)

description:

Sudoku rules: Normal sudoku rules apply.  The shaded cells form killer sudoku cages, the sum of which is clued in the top left of the region. The cell with the sum total is not necessarily part of a tetromino and, as usual, digits cannot repeat in a cage.

title: Can This Puzzle Make You Cleverer?
description:
Today we feature one of those puzzles that just makes us sit back in awe at the skill of the constructor, Jesper Josefsson.  It's called Cave Fillomino and has quite a complicated set of rules BUT it's 100% worth spending a couple of minutes to understand them - this is a BRILLIANT creation.  Play it here:


https://tinyurl.com/y4uxa62s


Rules:
Standard Fillomino rules apply ie divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions; each cell must contain a number equal to the number of cells in its region; no two regions of same size may share an edge. Hybrid Cave rules apply ie Some of the cells are to be shaded gray, so that all gray cells (the walls) are orthogonally connected to the edge, and all remaining cells form an orthogonally connected area (the cave); in an orthogonally connected area of gray cells, no numbers may repeat; each cell marked with a large circle is inside the cave, and its number indicates how many cave cells can be seen from it orthogonally (including the cell itself), given that walls obstruct the view; the top right cell is given as part of the wall, and therefore shaded gray from the start; it still needs a number in it.




**************************************************************

title: Monty Python And The Ghostly Trail:  The Sudoku!
description:
Today's puzzle is an incredible one (again) from Peter C Hayward continuing his John Cleese tributes!  You can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/tLmqnGRNPL


Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply.  The final grid will contain a 1-cell-wide python, which begins at the purple 1. The python may not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally. Numbers in blue squares show how many of its 8 surrounding squares are python. Blue squares cannot be python. All possible blue squares ARE given. (ie all possible cells that are not on the python but have the correct minesweeper total are given as blue). The final grid also contains a "ghost". The ghost is an identical copy of the python (shape, digits, orientation). Blue squares do not care about the ghost, only the original python. The ghost begins and ends on the original python. The ghost and python may overlap elsewhere as well.

title: We Love Pentominoes!
description:
Try Shye's stylish Pentominous Sudoku here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/PbmLMptRLN

Normal sudoku rules apply. Apart from the central cell, the grid must be fully tiled using nine different types of pentomino, rotated or reflected as necessary, but never sharing an edge with another of their own type. Numbers in the shapes follow these rules: L&U: contain unique digits; N&T: adjacent digits are non-consecutive; P&V: adjacent digits are consecutive; W&Y: contain unique digits that sum to a multiple of 3; Z: adjacent digits differ by more than 5.

title: Are You Smart Enough To Start?!
description:
Today we feature another puzzle by ukudos and it's a gem.  You can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/FBHPg2HqTN


Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue given in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits may not repeat within a cage. The purple line represents a 21-digit palindrome the ends of which have to be deduced (i.e. the first digit and the last digit lie adjacent to each other on the purple line).

[A palindrome is a sequence that reads the same backwards and forwards.  So, for a 10-digit number, 1234554321 would be a valid palindrome whereas 1234554221 would not be.]

title: A Puzzle To Rank Your Mensa IQ
description:
Today we feature a puzzle from the genius (and diabolical) mind of Phistomefel.  He calls it "Chaos Sudoku With Slitherlink #1".  You can play it here:
https://tinyurl.com/y267e524


Rules:
In every row, in every column and in every area, each number from 0 to 8 occurs exactly once. The boundaries of the areas for the irregular sudoku need to be located. If there is a circle in a cell, the number in it indicates how many of the neighbouring edges and corners are used for the area boundaries (the outer frame is counted for these purposes). So, for example, the circle in r4c9 MUST contain at least a 3 because the outer frame on its right involves two corners of r4c9's cell and one line segment joining these corners).


PLEASE CHECK THE LINK BELOW FOR ANY CLARIFICATION OF THE RULES (OR WATCH THE START OF THE VIDEO):

title: The Puzzle 50% Of You Voted For!
description:
We solve Quarterthru's Snake Sum sudoku. It's playable here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/9dpdgLft83

Normal sudoku rules apply except that the regions are irregular. Additionally, a snake has to be drawn into the grid. The head and tail of the snake are in the two cells with the grey circles. The snake may not touch itself orthogonally, but it can touch itself diagonally. The clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits located on the snake. Considering "Snake" and "non-snake" as two colors, the given digits show how many cells orthogonally connected to the given are of a different color to the color of the given cell itself. All such possible digits are shown. Givens can be on or off the snake.

title: What A Great Idea for a Sudoku
description:
Try Dying Flutchman's lovely Odd Pentomino/Killer/X-Sums sudoku here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/LhBdm9D7Nf
Normal sudoku rules apply and clues outside the grid give the sum of the first X digits seen in the row/column, given that X is the first digit seen from the clue. The grid must be filled with the 12 different pentominoes (allowing rotation/reflection), all of which cross a box boundary. Digits in shapes cannot repeat, and sum to an odd number for pentominoes, and an even number for tetrominoes. The three placed bar lines act as shape boundaries.

title: World Class Kakuro!
description:
Today we turn to the wonderful Kakuro puzzles of Prasanna Seshadri from his (very) recent competition on Logic Masters India (link below).  The two puzzles featured can be played here:


Puzzle 1:  https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/T9Jd3mF9LN
Puzzle 2:  https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/d2pd4JrtgL


Rules:
Basic Kakuro (Puzzle 1)
Enter a single digit from 1 to 9 into each white cell so that the sum of digits in each Across entry equals the value given to the left of the entry, and the sum of digits in each Down entry equals the value given above the entry. No digit may be repeated within a single entry.


Kakuro Variant (Puzzle 2)
As for puzzle 1 but, additionally, some cells are shaded and the digits in these shaded cells also act as Kakuro clues for subsequent white cells (ie until the next grey cell, black cell or grid boundary). It is up to the solver to determine if the shaded cell digit is an across or a down clue and it could be both. 



Link to contest:
https://logicmastersindia.com/2020/09P/

title: Yajisan Kazusan Sudoku - What Does It Mean?!
description:
Today's video features two puzzles!  One is an introduction to Yajisan Kazusan by Mokuani and the other is a sudoku hybrid based on YK - by Madmahogany.  You can play the puzzles at the following links:


Mokuani: http://pzv.jp/p.html?yajikazu/10/10/o42i42d1232c432323b22b23h13a13d23b33f22a12zb
Madmahogany: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/LN2QP3L8rD


Rules:
Basic Y-K rules (Puzzle 1):  Shade some cells such that: shaded cells must not be orthogonally adjacent; cells with digits can be shaded; a digit in an unshaded cell indicates the number of shaded cells in the corresponding direction; a digit in a shaded cell does not necessarily indicate the correct number of shaded cells; all unshaded cells must form a single orthogonally connected area.
Sudoku Rules: (Main Puzzle) Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with arrows are the Yajisan-Kazusan clues except that the valid clues give the sum of all the shaded cells in that direction (ie NOT the number of shaded cells).  All other basic Y-K rules apply.

title: Multiple Role Sudoku
description:
Try Daniel Galao Birkmann’s minimalist Multiple Role Sudoku here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Jr4LQRpR4M  

Normal sudoku rules apply and digits must increase along thermos. Numbers outside the grid act as X-Sums, sandwich clues, AND skyscraper clues. Identical digits cannot be a knight’s move apart. title: The Puzzle Of The Popular Vote
description:
Today's puzzle is a superb little starbattle/loop-drawing hybrid by the constructor Volatility.  You can play it here:
https://tinyurl.com/y5ord7hj


Rules:
Place two stars in each row, column and region so that stars do not touch, not even diagonally. Stars may not be placed on squares with a moon or sun. Draw a closed loop in the grid which passes through each region exactly once. The loop must pass through EITHER all moon cells OR all sun cells in any region; if the loop passes through moon cells in one region then, in the next region it enters, it has to pass through the sun cells, and vice versa. The loop must pass through at least one moon or sun cell in each region. The loop may not pass through stars.

title: A Certain Uncertainty
description:
Try JoJoMcFroYo's tricky Uncertainty Thermo Sudoku here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/rnMt4Ltpt7

title: Spacewar Sudoku
description:
Today's puzzle is a cool hybrid puzzle mixing starbattle, spiral galaxies and sudoku.  It's by the constructor Nell Gwyn and you can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/n774mt48GG


Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The dots are the centers of rotationally-symmetric cell groups (called "galaxies"), whose digits sum to the number beside the dot. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy and galaxies may not overlap. Each row, column and 3x3 box contains exactly two digits (no more, no less) that are not part of any galaxy. Those digits that are not part of a galaxy are "lone stars," and may not touch other lone-star digits orthogonally or diagonally.

Prasanna Seshadri’s new competition can be found here

title: No Given Digits!  No Cage Totals!  How??!
description:
Today's sudoku is quite quite extraordinary.  Willy Wonka has once again excelled himself and you can try the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/t2GN7MLRDB

Rules:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Outlined regions are cages, digits cannot repeat in these regions. The sum of the digits in a cage is called the "cage total".  A white dot exists between all cages where the cage totals have a difference of 1. A black dot exists between all cages where the cage totals have a ratio of 2. Note that there is a negative constraint ie all of the possible dots have been given.

title: The 13 Minute Sudoku Barrier
description:
Today's puzzle is by Akash Doulani from his new book World Of Sudoku (link below).  One of the world's best solvers, Freddie Hand, took 12mins 51secs to solve it.  Can you do better?  You can play it here:


https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/GqNML4m32D


Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. If the sum of digits in two orthogonally adjacent cells is 10 then they are separated by an X. If the sum of digits in orthogonally adjacent cells is 5 then they are separated by a V. All possible X & V are marked (which means if two orthogonally adjacent cells are not separated by an X or a V then they cannot sum up to 10 or 5).

title: A Puzzle Odyssey - Part 2 (Sound Improved)
description:
[We have had horrible sound issues this evening.  This should work...]

Today's brilliant puzzle is not THAT hard but it does require a LOT of precise logic.  It's called Japanese Sums With Pentominos by Uhu and it's a really fabulous piece of work...  Unfortunately Simon isn't on top form - which makes this a long one!

Try the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/4RBQDTHFfn

Rules:In the grid, some cells must be blackened and digits from 1 to 9 must be entered in the remaining cells so that no number occurs more than once in any row or column. The numbers outside the grid indicate the sums of blocks of connected digits in the correct order.  (The sum can be just a single digit).  All numbers 2, 3, 5 and 8 are given for the clues outside of the grid. A dot stands for any other number from 0 - 9. A two-digit sum cannot begin with a '0' (and must therefore be at least equal to 10).  In addition, the black cells form pentominos.  The finished grid must contain exactly twelve pentominos comprising the complete set of possible 5-cell shapes: FILNPTUVWXYZ. The pentominos may not touch,  even diagonally.

title: Colour By Numbers
description:
Today's puzzle is a lovely little LITS logic puzzle by Freddie Hand.  Don't worry if you've never seen one of these before - the rules are pretty straightforward!  Try it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/LLF6BNMnJL


Rules: 

Shade exactly four connected cells in each outlined region, to form an L, I, T, or S tetromino, so that the following conditions are true: (1) All shaded cells are connected with each other; (2) No 2×2 group of cells can be entirely shaded grey; (3) When two tetrominoes in adjacent regions share an edge, they must not be of the same type (L, I, T, or S), regardless of rotations or reflections.
[See the video if you are unsure what an L, I, T or S tetromino looks like.]

title: What Happens when Mark DOESN'T get Lucky
description:
Try Genomico’s Six-pack Linked Sudokus here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Rpq6Nrrj8T 
This is one large puzzle, consisting of six different variants of 6x6 sudokus, all linked together by circles. A circle is an outside clue for both adjacent puzzles.
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply to all sudokus, so each row, column and region must contain 1-6. Outside clues per variant show:
Difference Sudoku: The difference of the first two digits in the corresponding direction.
Outside-2 Sudoku: Must be placed in one of the first two cells in the corresponding direction.
Next-to-6 Sum Sudoku: The sum of all direct neighbours of the digit 6 in the row or column.
Skyscraper Sudoku: The number of visible skyscrapers from that side. Higher skyscrapers block the view of lower ones, size being given by the digit.
MaxAscending Sudoku: The length of the longest series of ascending digits in the corresponding direction. (E.g. the length of a 1-3-6 series is 3.)
First seen odd/even Sudoku: If odd, the first odd number in the corresponding direction; or, if even, the first even number.

title: Normal Sudoku Rules Do NOT Apply
description:
[Sorry for the late release this evening - YouTube kept freezing on 95% of the video "processed" so we've had to repeat the upload three times (so far).]


Today we feature a quite incredible puzzle by spxtr. It's called Fillomino Sudoku and the rules need careful attention! Try it here: 

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/HQGn6PG27m


Rules: Normal sudoku rules DO NOT APPLY except for the positions of the digits 3, 4, and 5 which must be entered once in each row/column/3x3 box. These are the ONLY digits that should appear in the grid. In addition, the grid is completely and uniquely covered with polyominos of size 3, 4, and 5. All 3, 4, and 5 digits entered in the grid are within a polyomino of their size. Polyominos of the same size cannot share an edge. A polyomino may contain more than one of the entered digits (ie 3s/4s/5s) if allowed by the previous rules.

description:

 Normal sudoku rules apply. Little killer (Arrow) clues show the sum of the indicated diagonal. title: How To Solve A Puzzle You've Never Seen
description:
Today we try something a bit different in response to a viewer suggestion!  The puzzle is Country Road by Jonas Gleim and Simon has doesn't think he's ever done one of these puzzles before.  You can try the puzzle here:
https://tinyurl.com/y58nj7b7

[If you select "Composite" you can select "Loop" from the new menu and then select Lineox to have a useful loop drawing tool]

Rules:
Draw a closed loop that consists of horizontal and vertical lines between cells (from cell centre to cell centre), and that doesn’t cross or touch itself. The loop visits each boldly outlined area exactly once. Clues indicate how many cells within an area are used by the loop. Non-loop cells are not allowed to touch orthogonally if they are in different areas.  [Also see the video for an example puzzle.]

title: But Could Batman Have Solved This Riddle?
description:
Check out our twitter thread on #TheRiddler's enigma in #TheBatmanTrailer:
https://twitter.com/crypticcracking/status/1297630422889828354

Today's puzzle is a twist on Kropki by Greg Dyer and it's sublime!  You can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/98mgtmGrdh

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply.  In addition difference and ratio clues are given:
Adjacent cells whose digits are a multiple of one another are marked with a grey circle, the ratio of which is inside the circle. Adjacent cells whose digits are different by a certain amount are given by a white circle, the difference of which is inside the circle.  Not all possible white and grey circles have been given. Numbers have been replaced by letters A-J (not including I) which represent the numbers 1-9. No number is represented by more than one letter.

Link to the puzzle on Logic Masters Germany:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003YK

*********************************************************************

title: An Impossible Work Of Genius
description:
Today's puzzle brings a tear to our eye such is the extraordinary beauty that Christoph Seeliger has incorporated into this puzzle.  This one video has more sudoku tricks than you can shake a stick at!  Try the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/MD22p7gMRT

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are some Killer Sudoku clues given. They are part of a group of connected cells and give the sum of the digits in this group. Digits may not repeat within these groups and groups for different clues cannot overlap. Each group is completely contained in one coloured orbit of the puzzle grid. Otherwise, placement and size of the groups is not known. There may be cells that are not part of any group.

title: The Devil's Jigsaw
description:
Phistomefel returns today but not with a sudoku.  He has constructed an incredible problem that even seems to affect Simon's computer!  You can try it here:
https://tinyurl.com/y22mojbw

There is an example of how the puzzle works at this link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=00044H

Rules:
Every cell of the grid has to be part of exactly one pentomino. Orthogonally adjacent pentominoes have to be different from each other (i.e. they cannot be transformed into each other by reflection and/or rotation). In addition, a round trip has to be drawn into the grid. It runs horizontally and vertically between the centers of cells. It may not cross or touch itself. A clue in a cell indicates how many cells of the according pentomino are passed through by the round trip. Every pentomino contains at most one clue. A pentomino without a clue has to be visited by the round trip at least once.

*********************************************************************

As mentioned in the video, Phistomefel has also just published a Starbattle puzzle.  You can find the puzzle here.  We will release a video on this puzzle for all our patrons on Patreon over the weekend.

title: A Sudoku That Defies The Laws Of Nature?
description:
Today's puzzle can't exist can it?  Prasanna Seshadri has set a sudoku that defies belief.  Play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/PtjrqnTpPB

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each digit inside the grid and its perimeter (rows 0&10 and columns 0&10) represents the height of the Skyscraper in that cell. Taller Skyscrapers hide shorter ones (and ones of the same size). The numbers beside diagonal lines give the number of Skyscraper clues seen in the corresponding directions in rows0&10 and columns 0&10 respectively and all the digits placed there give the number of Skyscrapers seen in the corresponding row or column inside the grid. A clue in a circle is the sum of the digits in the two cells on either side of the clue.  [For the avoidance of doubt:  the perimeter cells do not obey the rules of sudoku ie they can repeat.  So eg along r10 it would be fine for digits to repeat.]

[Please note that the "Check" button in the web app won't work properly for this puzzle as we had to build an 11x11 grid!]

title: The Problem Carlsen And Nakamura Haven't Solved (Yet)
description:
Today's puzzle is an absolutely incredible construction from HalfBakedLunatic.  You can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/MFRLnfBMqj

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply
Kings are 1s, Rooks are 2s, Bishops are 3s, Knights are 4s.
Basically, no King can be "in check".
[In detail: No two Kings can be a “Kings Move” apart; No King can be a “Knight’s Move” from any Knight; No King can be on the same diagonal as a Bishop, unless a Knight or a Rook is blocking the path; No King can be in the same row or column as a Rook unless a Knight or a Bishop is blocking the path.]
Along thermometer shapes, digits must increase from the bulb end.  Clues with arrows outside the grid indicate the sum of the cells along the indicated diagonal.  Digits can repeat along these diagonals.

title: Can You Spot This Cryptic Crossword's Hidden Theme!?
description:
You can play this lovely puzzle by Maize free at the following link:

https://puzzles.independent.co.uk/games/cryptic-crossword-independent/?puzzleDate=20200804#!202008




SPOILER:  (Explanations of certain clues):

Ramsey is a coastal town on the Isle Of Man
A person from Porlock is an unwanted intruder - named after such a person who interrupted Samuel Taylor Coleridge during his writing of the poem Kubla Khan.  So the clue is an allusion to the lines in that poem:

In Xanadu did Kubla Khan
A stately pleasure-dome decree:
Where Alph, the sacred river, ran
Through caverns measureless to man
     Down to a sunless sea.

A Galaxy is a large military US plane.

XD does look like a smiley face :)

title: Fawlty Towers - The Sudoku
description:
This is such a brilliant idea from Peter C Hayward, who made this as a tribute to the great John Cleese.  You can play the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/drtq6RH6TF

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Additionally, there are 9 towers. Digits in each tower sum to the number shown below it.Digits in each tower increase in value from bottom to top.  Except...2 of the towers are faulty, and do not increase in value, while another 5 towers do not sum to the given number. No tower is faulty in both ways.

Peter's discussion with John Cleese can be seen here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P0oHGT6ChRE

title: The Magic Behind The Miracle Sudoku
description:
Today's puzzle has been requested by many of you and it's a doozy.  Play spxtr's debut puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/nmrpHGn4FR

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply.
Nonconsecutive: any two orthogonally adjacent cells cannot contain consecutive digits.
Sandwich: the clues outside the grid show the sum of the numbers sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column.
Killer: cages show the sum of all the digits in the cage. Digits may not repeat in a cage

***************************************************************
We've recorded a short video for our Patrons explaining how to find the solution to Scott Strosahl's beautiful playing-card-themed Compass puzzle! 
Become a patron at:
https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

You can play Scott's puzzle here:
https://tinyurl.com/y6uj669k  

Rules: 
- Divide the grid into regions based on the given clues. 
- There will be one orthogonally connected 13-cell region for each suit, plus 2 Joker cells that are not in a region. 
- For each given clue, the numbers indicate how many cells are north, south, east, or west of the clue cell. 
- Joker cells may not be on the edges of the grid and must be rotationally symmetric around the center.

description:

title: A Sudoku With A 100% Rating
description:
Today's puzzle is by Stephane Bura and it has a perfect rating on Logic Masters Germany!  You can play the puzzle here:

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/gmj9DJPFGh

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Two arrows of the same colour pointing toward one another in a row, a column or a diagonal indicate the presence of a sandwich. The cells containing the arrows are the boundaries of the sandwich and these cells are also the digits of the sum of all the cells between these boundaries, in any order. A cell can be a boundary for several sandwiches in the same line. Digits may repeat in diagonal sandwiches.

description:
Today's puzzle by RockyRoer is one of the best puzzles for "teaching" sudoku geometry we've ever seen.  You can play the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Qd4drHbRJ3

To play the "Teaser" puzzle shown at the beginning click this link:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/TFfmNNQRpb

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits cannot repeat in cages but the cage totals will need to be deduced.  Each colored ring contains cages that all have the same total. However, the totals may differ from ring to ring. In addition, the sum of the numbers in each colored ring will appear in the rectangular outlines.

title: Digital Root Sudoku
description:
Try Rubik Nanota's Digital root Sudoku here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/RN3m2Nbbjm
Normal sudoku rules apply, digits do not repeat in cages and cage sums are shown by their digital roots, e.g. the digital root of a cage containing 2/3/8/9 is 4 as 2+3+8+9=22, and 2+2=4.

title: ヤジリン Sudoku = Jaw-Dropped
description:
This puzzle is am absolute marvel!  Solve Madmahogany's Yajilin Sudoku at the link below:
https://bit.ly/2Bgx2bW

If you'd like to play a Yajilin puzzle first then you can find one here:
http://pzv.jp/p.html?yajilin/10/10/c422020e41k23m21a3440h3040h3044a43m13k11e101032c

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Place some blocks in the grid. Digits in grey cells will be the clues for the number of blocks in the given direction. Blocks cannot touch orthogonally. The remainder of the grid (not blocks or clues) must be a part of a single continuous non-intersecting loop. Also, the loop can only turn in a cell containing an odd digit.

title: Mensa Sudoku
description:
One of our testers thinks this sudoku puzzle by Sumanta Mukherjee tests a lot of different aspects of "intelligence": numeracy, spacial awareness, logic.  What do you think?
Try the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/BLLGjtrb4P

Here is a version without any colouring in the grid:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/TMfdRGNFh7

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue given in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat in a cage.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of cells along the indicated diagonal.  Inequality signs in the grid point to the lower of the two cells involved.

title: Man vs Genius
description:
Oh dear... Simon decides to take on Phistomefel's latest masterpiece (100% rating on Logic Masters Germany and 5/5 for difficulty).  This sudoku is utterly gorgeous but our man finds it brutally difficult.  Will the man solve it or will the setting genius prevail? You can try the puzzle here:

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/hDNMJqPmTh

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid must be decomposed into different areas. Each cell belongs to exactly one area. Each area contains exactly two clues. The sum of all digits in an area lies between the two clues, but may not reach them. For example, if the clues for an area are 21 and 24, the sum of the digits in the area is 22 or 23. Digits may not repeat within an area.

The puzzle was published originally here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003DF

title: Try An Amazing Poker Puzzle!
description:
It's puzzle time today where we take a look at two Fillomino puzzles - one of which has a Poker theme!  You can play the puzzles at the links below:

Puzzle 1 (standard fillomino) by Murat Can Tonta:
https://tinyurl.com/yybn5s93

Puzzle 2 (poker fillomino) by Freddie Hand
https://tinyurl.com/y95cepq5 

Rules:
Standard Fillomino rules (puzzle 1):
Divide the grid along the dotted lines into regions called polyominoes so that no two polyominoes with the same area share an edge. Inside some cells are numbers; each number must represent the area of the polyomino it belongs to. A polyomino may contain zero, one, or more of the given numbers. (It is possible for a “hidden” polyomino — a polyomino without any of the given numbers — to contain a value that is not present in the starting grid.)

Poker Fillomino rules (puzzle 2)
Standard Fillomino rules (ie the rules above!). In addition, the numbers in the cages must form these hands in any order: four of a kind, straight, full house, three of a kind, one pair, one pair. Use the conversion 1 = ace, 11 = jack, 12 = queen, 13 = king.

Puzzle 1 featured on gmpuzzle.com this week here:
https://www.gmpuzzles.com/blog/2020/07/fillomino-by-murat-can-tonta-6/#comments
Puzzle 2 featured on our fan discord server here:
https://discord.com/channels/709370620642852885/720762591827460209/738745293247610981

title: Poker Sudoku
description:
Today's puzzle is by the creator of The Miracle Sudoku, Mitchell Lee and we absolutely love it.  You can play Poker Sudoku at one of the links below:
Version 1 (as Simon uses in the video):
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/R4HpPfGh4g

Version 2 (no colours):
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/J9rbjm4QnD

Version 3: (Penpa version)
https://tinyurl.com/yamckx7p

Reference for determining which poker hand is best:
https://www.fgbradleys.com/et_poker.asp

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  1 is treated as a poker ace. A greater-than symbol joining two cages indicates which cage is the higher-ranking hand in poker. Digits MAY repeat in a cage but cards may not repeat in a cage (but they may repeat in the grid). Eg a cage may not contain two cells with the 3 of hearts , but there may be two cells in the grid that both contain the 3 of hearts . Treat the cards and values exactly as you would in a game of poker. For example, an ace (1) ranks higher than any other card, but can be used as part of the lowest-ranking straight or straight flush: 12345. On the other hand, 6789A is not a straight.

Note:  this puzzle was the best puzzle from July's "Monthly Puzzle Prompt" competition on our Discord server, which was themed on Playing Cards.  August's competition theme is Stars and Stargazing.  You can find our fan Discord here:

title: Cracking The Cryptic:  The Movie
description:
Today Simon attempts a puzzle by ahaupt that will go down in sudoku history:  this goes beyond anything we've ever seen in a sudoku before and involves some completely new logic.  Unfortunately, as you'll see, it takes Simon quite a long time to find the logic in question!!  Play the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/pnf623FF7B

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
Group Sums: A number in a small circle indicates the sum of the digits in the cells covered by the corresponding circle. These digits may or may not repeat. Arrow Sudoku: Digits along an arrow must sum to the number in the corresponding circle. In this Sudoku all group sum clues contain a comparison operator. The clue ≥26 for example indicates a sum of at least 26. An arrow between two cells points to the smaller number.

title: Puzzles Like This Are Why We Love Sudoku
description:
Alexander Rappa returns to Cracking The Cryptic with this gorgeous (and very approachable) puzzle - play it at the link below:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/N6Jdp8Ndgp

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid function as BOTH Sandwich and X-Sums Clues. In addition, Queen and King sudoku rules apply.
1.  X-Sums: Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding direction. X is the first digit in the corresponding direction.
2.  Sandwich: Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9.
3.  King: No digit can lie a "king's move" away from an equal digit (i.e. no digit can be adjacent to an equal digit, even diagonally).
4.  Queen: You cannot repeat the number 9 within a "queen's move" (ie along the same diagonal).

The puzzle was published on Logic Masters Germany here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003ZH

title: Dutch Sudoku Magic
description:
Today's puzzle is a world-class hybrid sudoku by Hans van Stippent.  You can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/39j3M9MMPb

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules. Also, normal skyscrapers rules apply ie each number in the grid represents the height of a building and the clues on the outside of the grid indicate how many buildings can be “seen” when looking from that direction. Taller buildings block the view of smaller buildings. Additionally, the cells in grey are “underground” and cannot be seen for any of the outside skyscraper clues.  As an example, the 2 in row 2 refers only to seeing two buildings in columns 3 through 7, even if there is a 9 in column 1 or column 2 as that 9 cannot be seen.

description:

title: Can You Spot Simon's Error Before He Does!?
description:
This is a brilliant and difficult puzzle by Osh Tirola - which combines three different puzzle forms!  And Simon gets the blues from a mistake it takes him some minutes to spot!!

Play the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/GM8FdqTnMb

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. In each row/column/9-cell irregular region, two digits must be shaded as "stars".  These shaded cells cannot touch each other, even diagonally. Purple clues give the sum of the digits in the two shaded cells in their row/column. Grey clues give the sum of the digits sandwiched between the stars in their row/column.

title: This Sudoku Is As Good As It Gets
description:
Phistomefel has again created a sublime work of puzzle art with his Cave Sudoku.  Play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Hph4Qn9fB9

Rules:  [It is worth taking a quick look at the example solution at the link below as the rules are not too complicated once you "see" an example.]
Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, some cells must be colored grey so that all grey cells (the "walls") are orthogonally connected to the edge and all other cells form an orthogonally connected area (the "cave"). Each yellow marked cell is inside the cave and its digit indicates how many cave cells can be seen horizontally and vertically before hitting a wall or the edge of the grid. The clue cell itself is counted for this purpose.  The digit in some yellow cells has yet to be determined and not every possible clue cell is given. In an orthogonally connected area of grey cells no digits may repeat.  2x2 blocks of either cave or wall are possible.

Example solution (and original post of the puzzle):
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003U6

title: The 98% Sudoku
description:
Do give this wonderful puzzle by Bismuth a try - it isn't too hard but is an extremely enjoyable puzzle to solve.  You can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/FRgj24r4N9

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The circles in the grid are the centers of rotationally symmetric “galaxies”. Every cell in the grid is part of a galaxy. Digits may not repeat in a galaxy. The number by each circle represents the sum of the digits in that galaxy. Galaxies treat the grid as a torus, that is, rows 1 and 9 are adjacent, and columns 1 and 9 are adjacent.

The puzzle was published on our Discord server and also on Logic Masters Germany here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003TV

title: A Birthday Present Puzzle
description:
It's puzzle time today with this clever hybrid puzzle by Prasanna Seshadri which he's made as a birthday present for his fellow-moderator-of-our-discord-server Priyam Bhushan.  It's Priyam's birthday on 22 July - so many happy returns from Cracking The Cryptic!

[The rules printed on the video screen should be very slightly expanded:  the 2 and 6 are treated as in  a Star Battle puzzle so cannot touch themselves or each other ORTHOGONALLY as well as diagonally.]

You can play the puzzle here:  
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/MbpB7JGfnq

Rules:  
Place the letters A,B,D,H,I,M,P,R,Y and/or the digits they are assigned to in every row and column. (NOTE no 3x3 boxes!)The nine letters used in the puzzle represent a different number from 1-9. The letters outside the grid are all Skyscraper clues. ie each number represents the "height" of a skyscraper in that cell.  Numbers outside the grid indicate the number of visible skyscrapers from the direction (where taller buildings obscure smaller buildings "behind" them). After substitution within the grid, the digits 2 and 6 are "stars", and cannot touch orthogonally or diagonally with other instances of themselves or each other. The numbers outside the grid give the number of cells between the stars in that row. Stars cannot be on cells with red squares.  Red squares give a message in the finished grid. Grey Circles contain odd digits and grey squares contain even digits.

title: One Of THE Great Sudoku Puzzles
description:
This is one of THE great number-placement puzzles we've ever been sent.  Alice has made another startlingly brilliant sudoku and you can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/jfn8GP4LBQ

[Alice also thanks Yosh for giving some inspiration/ideas relating to the creation of this puzzle (in particular the N-shaped arrangement of given digits)].

Rules:  Each row, column and 9-cell region must contain all digits from 1 to 9. Additionally, each digit must see one or more identical digits by a chess knight's single move. For example, if cell R1C2 has value of 7, then at least one of cells (potentially many) R3C1, R3C3 or R2C4 must also contain a 7.

title: An Utterly Brilliant Tribute Puzzle
description:
Alexander Rappa's latest puzzle almost defeats Simon... you can try it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/NNL8HBpHLp

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The circles given in the grid are the centers of pointsymmetric "galaxies", which function as cages for the Killer Sudoku. The numbers inside the circles indicate the sum of the digits in the cages. In addition, each cage is a "thermometer". Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end, but the bulb end is not given. The cages/thermometers cannnot "branch".  Thermometers are also symmetrical about their circles. The digits in a cage/thermometer may not repeat. Not every cell in the grid has to be part of a galaxy.

title: Jekyll and Hyde Sudoku
description:
Here is a quality debut sudoku by Shye - you can play the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/rNhrQRPdD2

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  Cells separated by dots have the same common difference (green for one difference; red for another).  Outer clues are grouped in pairs; in each pair, one clue is a sandwich clue and the other is an x-sums clue.  A sandwich clue gives the sum of the cells sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column.  An x-sums clue gives the sum of the first X digits placed in the corresponding direction, where X is equal to the first digit placed in that direction. Some outside clues use dots in their equations: these are  multiplication or "to the power of", not concatenation. Not all possible clues are given IE no negative constraints operate.

title: A Sudoku by YouTuber 12tone!
description:
We're delighted to bring you this fresh take on Chess Sudoku from the brilliant YouTuber 12tone - it's called Knight's Court and you can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/jmBGMQJFbm

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. In addition, the central box (marked in green) is full of knights: Each cell in that box must see exactly one cell with the same digit by knight's move (in chess). All cells outside of the central box are not knights, and thus do not see any cells with the same digit by knight's move (except potentially in the central box.)

title: The Enigma Variations
description:
You can try this awesome follow-up to Big Tiger's Battlefield Sudoku from the constructor Carrick22 here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/2gNGNPdtHP

Rules:  Consider the first X cells and the last Y cells of a row or column where X is the number in the first cell and Y is the number in the last cell. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits where these groups overlap, or the sum of the digits in the gap between the groups if they don't overlap. A cell is colored red if it's part of an overlap in its row AND in its column. It's green if it's part of a gap in its row AND in its column. In this puzzle all clues are encrypted: each letter from A-J must be paired with a number from 0-9. Different letters are different numbers.  Digits in cages must sum to the clue in the top left of a cage. The number AB represent the number for which A is the tens digit, and B the units. It does not means A*B.

title: One Of THE Great Opening Sudoku Tricks
description:
Today's puzzle by Madmahogany makes for just an awesome solving experience!  You can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/tNrLppJNF7

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  In addition, both marked diagonals contain the digits 1-9 exactly once. If two consecutive digits are adjacent in the completed grid, the edge between them is marked with a white dot. Similarly, if two digits along the two main diagonals are consecutive, they have been separated by a grey dot. All possible white and grey dots are provided. If two cells contain the same digit, the "taxicab distance" cannot be equal to that digit. The "taxicab distance" is the minimum number of orthogonal moves from cell A to cell B.  For example, if there is a 4 in R3C4, there cannot be a 4 in R2C7, since it takes a minimum of 4 moves to go from R3C4 to R2C7.

title: 4th Of July Sudoku Fireworks
description:
Alexander Rappa has created this beast of a puzzle to celebrate Independence Day!  Try it here:

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/4hNFmTLrFb

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, each unique letter of "FOURTH OF JULY" represents a unique digit from 1-9. The two-letter sandwich clue represents a two-digit number where the first letter is the tens digit and the second letter is the units digit. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells "sandwiched" between the 1 and 9 in the relevant row/column.

*********************************************************************
You can watch Rob Stephenson and Maff Pott's video discussing sudoku and mental health here:
https://twitter.com/crypticcracking/status/1279441041586782210

Rob is a founder of InsideOut which helps address the stigma of mental ill-health in the workplace by publishing a list of senior business leader role models.
https://inside-out.org/

Maff is the founder of Camerados, a social enterprise that creates "public living rooms" in communities - places that people can go to support each other around their mental wellbeing.
https://www.camerados.org/

title: The Tau Sudoku
description:

Anyway, this is a really remarkable creation from Raf Coremans:  note that the first 24 digits of Tau appear in order in a circle clockwise around this grid - absolutely extraordinary.  Try the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/RNbpGThQTg

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  Within cages, digits cannot be repeated.  Every number in the grid is lying and must be one less or one greater than the given number. title: This Is The Sudoku We've Waited For!
description:

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/L9LQP67LPg

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply, Each cage forms a line with a one-cell width. The number on the top left of a cage shows the sum of the numbers sandwiched between the smallest number and the largest number of the line. Digits cannot repeat in cages. Digits have been encrypted such that each letter represents a unique digit.  Bold letters in cells indicate the digit that must appear in that cell in the solution. The number AB represent the number for which A is the tens digit, and B the units. It does not mean A*B.
