title: Akari Sudoku - A Brilliant New Puzzle
description:
A mixture of two of my favourite puzzles today, Akari and Sudoku.  This lovely hybrid is the work of Andrej Boban and you can play it here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/h7HNDjhjqf

Rules: Normal sudoku rules apply.  There are two “lightbulbs” (“LB”s) in the white cells of every row/column/3x3 box.  LBs illuminate the cell they are in, as well as their row/column up to the point the light hits a grey cell or the outer edge of the grid.  All white cells must be illuminated and a LB cannot illuminate another LB. Grey cells contain clues about positions of LBs:  if there are no LBs orthogonally adjacent to a grey cell, it must contain an 8 or a 9.  If there are 1,2,3 or 4 LBs orthogonally adjacent to a grey cell then it must contain a 1, 2, 3, or 4 respectively.  A LB will always have a value of 5,6 or 7.  Remaining cells that are not LBs or clues may have any value.

 ***************************************************************************

description:

title: Beyond Sudoku
description:
Today's puzzle is another Phistomefel tribute - this time from the young phenom from Hong Kong, Undar Beyond.  You can play the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/JfFBFHMHqG

Rules: Normal Sudoku rules apply. The circles shown in the grid are the centres of point-symmetrical “galaxies”. Each galaxy forms a line with one-cell width that must contain at least 3 cells.  Each line cannot touch itself and does not form any loop. Galaxies cannot overlap. The number next to a circle shows the sum of the numbers between the smallest and the largest number of the galaxy line. Numbers cannot be repeated along galaxy lines. Not every cell in the grid has to be part of a galaxy.  [Please watch the start of the video if you are unsure about what a galaxy means in the context of the puzzle.]

We have created a brand new sudoku puzzle hunt.  We'd been hoping to reach 1500 patrons on Patreon to release the hunt (which is just going through the final test-solver as we speak!).  Launch is imminent and we are so grateful to all of you who've joined our Patreon community over the last 24 hours. Please keep the patron numbers growing and we'll let you know as soon as we get the puzzle back from final testing.]

title: An Hour's Worth Of Pure Logic!
description:
We had a lot of requests following yesterday's video to try this puzzle - also by ahaupt.  Simon does his best but this is not easy... try it here:

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/njQnT9RpTR

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply except the nine regions aren’t 3x3 boxes but irregular shapes which need to be discovered. A number in the top left of a cell indicates the sum of the digits in that cell’s region that can be seen looking north, south, east and west from that cell (including the cell itself). Cells outside the same region obstruct the view. The cell with the clue in the top left counts only once in the sum.  There is also a useful example solution here:  https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003MW

title: How Good Is Your Logic?
description:
Today's puzzle is just so elegant and it's by the compiler Ahaupt.  We'd give this 6/10 for difficulty so it's approachable if you're new to sudoku variants:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/qjGQffjL6B

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply. Each number corresponds to a high-rise building of the appropriate height. If an arrow is shown in a cell, the number indicates how many high-rise buildings can be seen in this direction (from the ground). Larger buildings hide the smaller ones behind.  There is also a nice example puzzle here:  https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003H3

Here is a link to the latest round of the World Sudoku Grand Prix.  The next round of which takes place next weekend.  In the video I mention this is the German round, it is actually the German and Dutch round (which explains why Richard Stolk and Arvid Baars have contributed puzzles).  Apologies for this error.  The other two setters are Christoph Seeliger and Jonas Gleim.  So this contest's puzzles will be of an extremely high standard.

https://gp.worldpuzzle.org/content/sudoku-gp

title: How To Solve Advanced Nonograms!
description:
Shout out to Prasanna Seshadri for recommending the puzzles in today's video:

Grant Fikes:  https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/4R7H4Nh22N
Murat Can Tonta: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/RdgJhj88pF
Serkan Yurekli:  https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/4FfmrdfFRh

Rules:  Shade cells to create a single orthogonally-connected group of black cells.  No 2×2 region can contain all black cells. Numbers outside the grid represent the groups of consecutive black cells in that row/column in order, either from left to right or from top to bottom. A question mark (?) represents a single group of consecutive black cells whose size is unknown (but cannot be zero); an asterisk (*) represents any number of unknown groups of black cells, including none at all.

GM Puzzles produces puzzles under a CC licence (https://tinyurl.com/3pj3byec). No changes have been made to any of the puzzles in this video.

title: The Sudoku IQ Test
description:

Rules: This is a normal killer sudoku, in which the small digit in the top left of each cage denotes the sum of all the numbers in the cage. Numbers must not be repeated in the cage. However, if there is a 9 in a cage in this sudoku, the 9 is not included in the cage total.  For example, if [8 4] is in a cage, the total of the cage is 12, but in a cage with [9 3 4] it is 7.

title: One Grandmaster's Tribute To Another
description:
Here is Prasanna Seshadri's brilliant tribute to Phistomefel:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/29tgh3PGTm

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply except that the regions are irregular. Additionally, a snake has to be drawn into the grid.  The head and tail of the snake are in the two cells with the grey circles. The snake may not touch itself orthogonally, but it can touch itself diagonally.  In the correct solution, the cells without snake form exactly eight areas, one of each size from 1 to 8.  Such an area of size n contains each digit from 1 to n exactly once.

description:
Try Chiel Beenhakker's Aquarium puzzles celebrating Cracking the Cryptic's 3rd Birthday here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/nM4nBRHQJH and here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Bq6HJrg9p7
Aquarium Rules: Colour the grid green and blue so that, within a region, cells that are located in the same row are either all blue or green. In a region, when a row is blue, all cells below that must be blue as well. There can be fully green or blue regions.  Puzzle 1: Numbers outside the grid indicate how many cells are blue in the respective row and column.  'Over 3' may not mean a multiple of 3. All rows and columns must contain at least one blue cell. 

Puzzle 2: A clue N outside the grid means a change of colour must occur after the Nth cell in that row or column, seen from that direction. Zeros are cosmetic and do not mean anything. Regions entirely surrounded by cells of one colour must be the other colour. Every row and column must contain at least one green cell.


Puzzle 3 is at our Patreon site: Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

title: The Miracle Thermo Sudoku
description:
Today we feature a puzzle by Mitchell Lee (the genius behind The Miracle Sudoku!):
https://tinyurl.com/ybt66u3b

Rules: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, place the eight thermometers into the grid. The thermometers must be placed into the grid in their original orientation (see the puzzle link). They may not be rotated or reflected.
The thermometers may not overlap each other. However, they may overlap the given digits in the grid. Along each thermometer digits must increase starting from the bulb.

PATREON BONUS PUZZLE:  To celebrate 3 years since our first video upload (11 June 2017), Cheel Beenhakker has made a lovely themed Aquarium puzzle.  We've shared this today with our patrons on Patreon.  If you're interested in extra content, you can become a patron of the channel here:

title: Cracking The Cryptic does ASMR!
description:
We've had so many requests to do this that we decided to do it as a one-off.  I am told it is important that you listen with headphones.  Sorry if it isn't your cup of tea, we'll be back to normal at 11pm tonight!

Today we showcase another beautiful puzzle by Jesper Josefsson - who only made his debut a couple of days ago!  You can play the puzzle here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/RPdNfMq8FQ

Rules: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Clues are given on selected diagonals in the format T [S]: 
 - T is the total sum of the digits along the diagonal; 
 - S is the sum of the digits on the diagonal that are located between the highest and lowest digit present on that diagonal (but excluding those two digits); 
 - If S is given as a number (0 or greater), there is a unique highest digit and a unique lowest digit on the diagonal;  
 - If S is given as “-“, the sandwich sum is undefined, because the highest digit or the lowest digit (or both) repeat along the diagonal; 
 - sometimes the T clue is omitted and only the [S] part given.

title: Manhattan Sudoku
description:
Today's puzzle is pretty incredible and it's by Madhav Sankaranarayanan.  Please read the rules carefully - they are a little tricky today but the puzzle makes them worth understanding - it's a cracker :)
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/gpp2Jq3bRJ

Normal Sudoku rules apply. Diagonals must contain the digits 1-9 exactly once. The inequality sign points to the lower of the two cells it connects.  The black dot indicates that one of the connected cells must be double the other.  The "taxicab" distance between two cells is the minimum number of orthogonal moves required to go from cell A to cell B.  In the completed grid, ONLY the red cells contain digits that are their taxicab distance away from another cell containing the same digit.  For example, if cell A and B both contain 8 and had a taxicab distance of 8 between them then they MUST both be red.  No two white cells have this property.  Of the set of digits 1 to 9, only a subset (whose sum is less than 15) can appear in the red squares.

title: It Looks Easy But Can You Start This Puzzle?
description:

title: Is This Our Best Ever Solve?
description:
Do try this absolutely mesmerising puzzle by ahaupt - seriously, it's one of the best puzzles we've ever seen:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/TQgmLDQLd7

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits in cages must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Within cages, digits are “balanced” and the frequencies of the digits are “as equal as possible”. So in cages with sum ≤ 45, each digit occurs at most once, (ie normal killer sudoku).  In cages with sum 46 ≤ ... ≤ 90, each digit occurs either once or twice (not never!).  Additionally, cells that are a knight's move (in chess) apart must not contain the same digit.

title: Battlefield Sudoku
description:
Here is brand new type of sudoku - invented by BigTiger - by Christoph Seeliger.  Let us know if you enjoy it because we can then showcase BigTiger's original puzzle too :)

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/R7TPFq2ff4

RULES:  Normal sudoku rules apply.   Consider the first x and last y cells of a row/column where x is the value of the first cell and y is the value of the last cell. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits where these groups overlap or the sum of the digits between these groups.  PLEASE SEE THE PICTURE AT THE START OF THE VIDEO. title: Give Yourself A Few Minutes Of Puzzle Joy
description:
BBC Video:
https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/uk-england-gloucestershire-52868820/people-use-us-to-go-to-sleep-to-sudoku-solvers-become-internet-sensation

You can try Phistomefel's latest jaw-dropping sudoku here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/jh8B2BpF2g

This page on Logic Masters Germany has a useful example picture of how the puzzle works:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003K1

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, a snake has to be drawn into the grid. The head and tail of the snake are in the two cells with grey circles. The snake may not touch itself orthogonally, but can touch itself diagonally. The rest of the cells without the snake form exactly eight areas, one of each size from 1 to 8. Such an area of size n contains each digit from 1 to n exactly once.

title: The Hardest Sudoku Ever
description:
Here is an unutterably brilliant (and mind-bendingly hard) sudoku by Matyas Martinka.  The rules are a little complicated but it is worth studying them!
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/H9Jr7gQHtm

RULES:  Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cell in the grid should be coloured blue (for water) or green (for land). For cells containing arrows, the digit in that cell shows how many cells share the same colour with the cell in the given direction, NOT including the arrow cell itself. Note that these same-colour cells need not be connected to the arrow cell. Not all arrows are given. The water occupies a single orthogonally connected region of the grid but no 2x2 area can contain only water cells. An island is an orthogonally connected region of at least 3 land cells. All land cells must be part of islands (so land cells are always in groups of three or more orthogonally connected cells). Islands may touch each other diagonally. Land cells forming any island must contain different digits.

title: This Sudoku Tells Lies
description:
You can try this WONDERFUL puzzle by Prasanna Seshadri here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/8QDLTJG34f

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the number given in the top left of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat in a cage.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along these diagonals.  One of the digits from 1-9 is a joker – wherever it appears in the grid, it can count as any digit from 1-9 for cage and diagonal sums, and it can be DIFFERENT for both – but (as in normal killer sudoku) it can only appear once in each cage.

Stuff mentioned in today's video:
Scriptnotes Podcast with Craig Mazin (@clmazin) & John August (@johnaugust):
https://podcasts.google.com/feed/aHR0cDovL3NjcmlwdG5vdGVzLmxpYnN5bi5jb20vcnNz/episode/NmZmZGY1MjEtYjRkNS00ZWRhLWI1ZjEtMTY2ZmY1ZjA0ZmFj?hl=en-GB&ep=6

description:

title: Miracles Are All Very Well,  The Impossible Takes Longer!
description:
*Please read the Rules below*

You can try this brilliant (and brutal) puzzle by Osh Tirola here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/M8nf3Q7DJb

RULES:  [PLEASE read these rules carefully - we have slightly changed them from the description on the right-hand-side of the video to make them as clear as possible.  Please also see the example solution in the video, which should help explain how they work.]

Normal sudoku rules apply.  In each row/column/3x3 box, two digits must be shaded as "stars".  These shaded cells cannot touch each other, even diagonally.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits in the two shaded cells in their row/column.  In the finished grid, the digits 4 and 6 cannot touch each other (or themselves), even diagonally.

Kurt Hugo Schneider's "Nightmare" 6x6 puzzle is available free here:
https://www.patreon.com/posts/37223311

title: The Most Complex Sudoku Ever
description:
You can try Prasanna Seshadri's brilliant sudoku "Compounding The Co-Dependency" here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/TmMBJj8jbr

Rules: [See the page here: https://www.patreon.com/posts/37065725]

Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, there are some special CTC rules in this puzzle:  There are 7 pairs of variants in this sudoku, totalling to 14 different rules. For each pair, one area will follow one variant and the other area will follow the other variant. It is up to the solver
to determine which variant gets used where. Throughout there will be no converse rules like “all possible dots are given” etc.  Here are the pairs:

All clues on the left/All clues on the right:
A) Outside Parity – The clue gives the first N cells of the same parity until the first cell of the other parity in that direction.
B) Skyscraper – The numbers represent the heights of skyscrapers. The clues outside give the number of skyscrapers seen from that direction. Taller skyscrapers block shorter ones.

All clues on the top/All clues on the bottom:
A) Serbian Frame – The clue gives the sum of the digits in the 3rd and the 4th cells in that direction.
B) X-Sums – The digit in the first cell takes up the value of N where the clue outside gives the sum of the first N cells in that direction.

1st Box/ 9th Box:
A) Arrow – The digit in the circle must be the sum of the digits along the line.
B) Thermo – The digits must be in increasing order from the circle to the end of the line.

2nd Box/ 8th Box:
A) 3-Difference – The white dots mean that the digits on either side must have a difference of 3.
B) Consecutive – The white dots mean that the digits on either side must have a difference of 1.

3rd Box/ 7th Box:
A) Even Set – The shaded cells must contain 2, 4, 6 and 8 in any order.
B) Odd Set – The shaded cells must contain 1, 3, 5 and 7 in any order.

4th Box/ 6th Box:
A) Kropki – The white dots mean that the digits on either side must have a difference of 1. The black dots mean that of the two digits on either side, one must be double the other.
B) XV – The white dots mean that the digits on either side sum to 10. The black dots mean that the digits on either side sum to 5.

5th Box: There are two clues here and each of them will follow one of the two rules below.
A) Quadruple – The digits shown must appear in the 2x2 area of cells they are in the middle of.
B) Quad Sum – The number is the sum of all four digits in the 2x2 area of cells the clue is in the middle of.

title: How To Solve 'The Puzzle Of The Year'
description:
You can try the latest masterpiece from Phistomefel here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Qtd84QLnMr

Rules: Normal sudoku rules apply. The dots given in the grid are the centers of pointsymmetric 'galaxies' (ie orthogonally connected groups of cells), which function as cages for the killer sudoku. The number above a dot indicates the sum of the digits in such a cage. The digits in a cage may not repeat. Contrary to a "classic" spiral galaxy puzzle, not every cell in the grid has to be part of a galaxy.

title: The Devil's Hardest Puzzle
description:
And our longest ever sudoku video...!  You can try Phistomefel's Chaos Construction at the link below:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Tt9mr4T46n

HELP US!  We are trying to ensure that Mitchell Lee's extraordinary miracle sudoku is seen by as many people as possible.  If you have social media/reddit/etc where you would be prepared to share the video then let's make this puzzle famous!

https://youtu.be/yKf9aUIxdb4


Rules for Phistomefel:  The digits 1 to 9 need to appear exactly once in each row/column/region.  The regions need to be discovered!  An arrow in a cell indicates that an uninterrupted sequence of exactly X cells in the direction
of the arrow - beginning at the cell with the arrow - belong to the 
same region (X being the digit in the cell with the arrow).  If there
is another cell after the sequence of X cells in the direction of the 
arrow then this MUST belong to a different region.  Not all arrows
that would be possible with the shape of the regions are given.

title: The One Clue Sudoku
description:
You can try this beautiful sudoku by ProwlingTiger here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/Jj3bG8NGQF

Rules: Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal killer sudoku rules apply ie digits may not repeat within a cage. Normal little killer sudoku rules apply ie each arrow denotes the sum of the digits along that diagonal (and digits may repeat along the diagonal).  In this puzzle, each killer/little killer sum is equal to one of two numbers M or N (both of which need to be deduced). For example, the two sums could be 8 and 17; and therefore each cage and arrow sums to either 8 or 17.

title: A Sudoku Of Sublime Genius
description:
You can try this absolutely brilliant puzzle by Matyas Martinka here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/hg764Pd67f

[Please note the rules below seem more complicated than they are and this puzzle is well worth the effort of understanding them!]

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  Each cell in the grid should be coloured blue (for water) or green (for land). For cells containing arrows, the digit in that cell shows how many cells share the same colour with the cell in the given direction, NOT including the arrow cell itself. Note that these same-colour cells need not be connected to the arrow cell. Not all arrows are given. The water occupies a single orthogonally connected region of the 
grid but no 2x2 area can contain only water cells. An island is an orthogonally connected region of at least 3 land cells.  All land cells must be part of islands (so land cells are always in groups of three or more orthogonally connected cells).  Islands may touch each other diagonally.  Land cells forming any island must contain different digits.

title: Yoda's Sudoku:  Unlearn What You Have Learned
description:
See if you can unlearn what you've learned vs Nylimb's mind-bending Sandwich Sudoku:
https://tinyurl.com/ybyl6lv5

Rules:  Fill the grid with 1-digit and 2-digit numbers, so that every row, column, and 3x3 box contains each of the 10 digits, from 0 to 9, exactly once: Eight cells contain 1-digit numbers, and the other cell contains a 2-digit number (from 10 to 98).

Clues outside the grid give the sum of all numbers sandwiched between the largest and smallest numbers in that row or column. For example, if a row contains 4, 1, 5, 8, 2, 7, 60, 3, and 9, then the largest number is 60, the smallest is 1, and the sandwich sum is 5+8+2+7 = 22.

Note that you could reverse the digits of any 2-digit number in the grid (if it doesn't end with 0), without changing the sandwich sums. So there's an additional rule to avoid such ambiguity: In every 2-digit number the tens digit is larger than the ones digit; e.g. 73 can occur but 37 cannot.

title: The Eminen Sudoku
description:
You can try ProwlingTiger's debut puzzle on the channel here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/6948F3hqt4

Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the clue given in the top left corner of each cage.  Digits must not repeat within cages.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells along the indicated diagonal.  Digits may repeat within these sums.  In this puzzle, m and n represent (not necessarily distinct) integers. In other words, every m clue sums to the same number and every n clue sums to a same (but possibly different from m) number.

title: If It's Good Enough For James Charles...!
description:
You can try Ryan Oswald's cunning Snake Sandwich Sudoku here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/h2bfTLTQ3j

Normal sudoku rules apply.  Solvers can locate a 'snake' in the grid, starting in the top left 1 and finishing in the bottom right 9.  The snake is formed of orthogonally-connected cells in the sequence 123456789 and then repeating (ie back to 1,2, etc). It cannot intersect itself (but it can touch other cells on the snake).  The clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells "sandwiched" between the 1 and 9 in the row/column. 

Nicolas Rasmussen's puzzle hunt puzzle is available free here:

title: How Did Anyone Crack This Puzzle In 6 Minutes?!
description:
You can try the two Castle Wall puzzles featured in the video at the links below:
Ken Endo:  https://tinyurl.com/uayep59
VanillaIce:  https://tinyurl.com/y9fvq4eq

Thanks to Takuma Kitamura for his commentary on his solve of Ken's puzzle and to Ryotaro Chiba for the translation.

Castle Wall Rules:  Draw a single closed loop (without intersections or crossings) passing through some empty cells in the grid. Black cells must be outside the loop; white cells (with heavy borders) must be inside the loop.  Grey cells can be either inside or outside and you must work out which!  Numbers and arrows refer to the total count of the number of cell borders crossed by the loop in that direction.

Nicolas Rasmussen's puzzle hunt can be played for free here:

title: How To Beat The World's Fastest Puzzler
description:
A special video today featuring the race between Ryotaro Chiba and Ken Endo in the recent Heads-up Puzzle Championship.  You can try the Coded Tents puzzle by Takuma Kitamura here:

Please NOTE the rules of this puzzle as a number of early comments have illustrated that I could have made them clearer:
Each tent is attached to one tree (so there are as many tents as there are trees).
A tent can only be found horizontally or vertically adjacent to a tree.
Tents are never adjacent to each other (ie not even diagonally).
A tree might be next to multiple tents, but is only connected to one.
The encoded numbers down the side tell you how many tents are in the respective row.  Each letter represents a different number (which may be zero).

https://opt-pan.github.io/penpa-edit/?m=solve&


If you can't speak Japanese, please watch the video to understand the entry method!

title: Sandwich Sudoku (With Extra Ants!)
description:
You can try this clever variant from Scott Strosahl here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/mbpTBgtRmj
Standard sudoku rules apply.  Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits ‘sandwiched’ between the 1 and 9.  In addition, ants must navigate from the green cell to the red cell.  They always move the number of spaces indicated in the current cell, turn 90 degrees, and move the number of spaces in the new cell. Also, this path may not cross itself.

title: World-Famous YouTuber Creates Genius Sudoku
description:
You can try this brilliant puzzle by Kurt Hugo Schneider here:
https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/BjDnndmJF7


Rules:  Normal sudoku rules apply.  There are nine thermometers in the grid.  Five are normal (ie bulb end contains smallest digit and numbers go up from there); Four are broken (ie bulb end contains BIGGEST digit and numbers go down from there).  There are two thermometers that share a bulb (in row3column7) - these thermometers do not need to both be normal or both be broken, they could be one of each.


Kurt's YouTube channel is here:
https://www.youtube.com/user/KurtHugoSchneider
@KurtHSchneider
